entries.minimalAmendment: None to the grammar. Re-draft: SUPPORTING EXISTS items (AUTHORED from the V1 vocabulary's own definitions) on O1[kind=line], O1[kind=gate], S2[noun=zone & functionsâˆ‹objective-area] and P4[roleName=target player]; 11.b as an EXCLUSION on J11b forbidding an assignment that yields no live PRIMARY_SCORING member in the build-out episode. entries.reasoning: No guard is needed. FIELD items (05.a, 09.a/b) apply only where their carrier exists (RC-1). SUPPORTING existence supports without requiring (RC-28; Â§8 checks REQUIRED only); RPC-001's DNC calls target players 'permitted, never required'. entries.minimalAmendment: None. TYPICAL_EXAMPLE is inert (RC-28: no support, bound or collision), so the E1 = 15 condition and the P2/P5 pairing can stay in one item's value text with nothing lost. Do not adopt the drafter's selector fix: P5 has no selector, and a selector testing E1 is not over the element's own attributes, so it would change RC-1 matching, a hidden STRUCTURAL change.
entries.reasoning: The source is an example ('e.g., for 15 players: 6v6 + 3 neutrals, or 7v7 + 1 neutral'). Nothing evaluates an inert value, so there is nothing for a condition to gate. The slice envelope is 12, not 15, so the example would not apply anyway. The rule the pairing implies (neutrals inside the total) is NEUTRAL-10.a, in another theme. Only if Christian made the example a default would a guard on E1 be needed, and that would be STRUCTURAL.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Hold 05.a as SUPPORTING EXISTS on S2[functionsâˆ‹trigger] with valueStatus N/A (RC-6). It supports a trigger region if one is laid out and requires none. Where 05.b's REGION_ENTRY {trigger region} is chosen, Â§5.2's 'every region referenced anywhere exists' requires the region. Clarify RC-35: an unmatched SUPPORTING existence item is reported as not used, never VIOLATED.
entries.reasoning: Optionality comes from strictness, not valueStatus: SUPPORTING items support like REQUIRED ones, but Gate B checks only REQUIRED items (RC-28, Â§8). So RC-6's N/A does not make 05.a unconditional, and PREFERRED_DEFAULT/ADAPTED turns SD-08 (a displaced value) into a guard. The drafter is right that a true guard would be STRUCTURAL; none is needed. Slice: no trigger region, V17 unstated; no line moves, and 05.a's ADAPTED report becomes not used.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Hold 'can be introduced' as NON_CLAIMED on P2 (a permission is a non-claim), beside the inert TYPICAL_EXAMPLE I13, so a CLAIMED declaration with only an inert item cannot be read as barring free choice. 'When the goal is defending under overload' is selection knowledge: under SD-17, a session goal that wants asymmetry enters with its own contract requiring it.
entries.reasoning: The clause says when a variant suits a session goal, which is cross-object selection knowledge the spec keeps out (Â§7, SD-17). GF4 authors no symmetry, so there is no requirement to switch off. Had it authored a default, SD-08 already settles it: a PREFERRED_DEFAULT displaced by another contract is ADAPTED. 'In defending half' and which 'goal' is meant are KNOWLEDGE. I13 is inert, and GF4 is not in the slice.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: A guard: no contract item can apply only when another row holds a given value. The register has one only for SD-13 (its condition, read by RC-24). None of the four entries needs it. FIELD items apply only where their element exists; branch-dependent existence is held as SUPPORTING EXISTS, with the chosen branch made necessary by Gate A reference resolution; examples are inert; session-goal conditions are selection knowledge.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: No grammar change. One run-convention clarification: an unmatched SUPPORTING existence item is non-failing and creates no needed-but-unstated line (RC-15, RC-35). Optional LOCAL: an O1 functions attribute, as S4 has, so only a carrier used as a scoring reference draws support. A true item-level guard would be STRUCTURAL (support would depend on another line's verdict, as RC-24 does for SD-13) and should wait for a case that needs it.
themeVerdict.why: All four entries are held with existing strictness, selectors, Gate A and SD-08, and none changes a slice line verdict. Two drafter labels were wrong: #1 and #51 are not STRUCTURAL, and #25's proposed LOCAL fix hides a STRUCTURAL change to selectors. Watch item: if Christian authors a REQUIRED existence that holds in only one branch, and no reference makes Gate A require it, a guard would be needed, and that would be STRUCTURAL.

entries.minimalAmendment: None to the grammar. Hold the target as the objective: J1[role=PRIMARY_SCORING] EXISTS, J2 EQUALS {the target line object, the target zone region} (J2 is already typed 'object or region reference'), carriers bounded by O1[kind=line] RANGE 0..1 and S2[noun=zone & functionsâˆ‹objective-area] RANGE 0..1, both fillable rows. Or keep the drafter's S3 {zone, line} and send 'line' to the SD-18 noun review (VOCABULARY).

RC-29 then gives NOT_AUTHORED(ALTERNATIVES) on non-fillable J2, the same result as the drafter's S3 route. The chosen carrier is a count fill inside an authored 0..1. Tying the carrier to the V1 member (line_crossed or target_zone_entered) is theme A. No amendment is adopted, so nothing on the slice moves.

entries.minimalAmendment: None to the grammar. Keep V7 and V11 NOT_AUTHORED (selector-scoped, RC-13), naming the three options as what is missing, with the options as inert TYPICAL_EXAMPLE items. Christian rules whether they are closed and exclusive. 11.b reads UNMET on the slice because RC-35 reports a REQUIRED FIELD item that matches nothing (themes A and E); that is not this gap. entries.reasoning: The drafter's own ledger logs both premises as KNOWLEDGE: examples or closed options, and 'exactly one' (assumption #2). The authored part (an advantage is needed; its form is not authored) is a NOT_AUTHORED declaration, and RC-15 lists a missing advantage as needed. A cross-row set would give NOT_AUTHORED(ALTERNATIVES) on non-fillable V7/V11, which blocks just as DECLARED_GAP does now. C2's magnitude stays NOT_AUTHORED either way.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Keep I02 (O1[kindâˆˆ{goal,target}] COUNT 2) and add two EXCLUSION items: O1[kind=goal] COUNT 1 and O1[kind=target] COUNT 1 (forbidden values). WIDEZONE-16.b already uses COUNT with EXCLUSION this way on V0. Per-kind COUNT âˆˆ {0,2} does the same job. 'target' off the O2 list is VOCABULARY; what 'target' is stays KNOWLEDGE (drafter's I02 entry).
entries.reasoning: 'Two of one kind' constrains one collection; it is not an either/or between items. A total of 2, with exactly one of either kind forbidden, leaves only 2+0 or 0+2. EXCLUSION never supports, so derivation is untouched. Kinds stay only narrowed by âˆˆ and O2 is non-fillable, so NOT_AUTHORED(ALTERNATIVES), which is correct: GF4 names no default. The midline has to stay off O1 (I03 does this). GF4 is not in the slice. The STRUCTURAL label fails.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Restate the game with T3 = a player of the team T2 names (goalkeeper included) and T4 = that team's own half (own-half-A/B). The goalkeeper stands in its own half and T5 is STATIONARY_BALL in both arms, so the arms differ only in who takes the ball. RPC-001-16.b already holds the same wording on T3 alone, and so does A01-02-11.a. The unnamed second actor is KNOWLEDGE.
entries.reasoning: The 'or' is a permission to the restarting team. Which player takes a given restart is play, outside the boundary. T4 is the same in both arms, so nothing crosses rows. Every item that reaches these T3 lines is either ENGINE_ONLY (RPC-001-16.b) or ASSUMED on non-fillable T3 (A01-02-11.a). So L122, L131, L140, L147 and L154 stay unsupported however T3 is written. The drafter mis-split one alternative across two rows.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: An item-level disjunction: one authored alternative whose members sit on different rows or collections. Value sets hold alternatives only within one row. No entry here needs it. Each is held by the existing cross-kind J2 reference, by COUNT plus EXCLUSION on one collection, by vocabulary, by NOT_AUTHORED declarations, or by a superset value, and gets the same verdicts RC-29 would give.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: None to the grammar. Record it as restatement guidance, not a new mechanism. An either/or across rows is held in one of three ways: on one row where J2 or the vocabulary allows; as COUNT plus EXCLUSION items on one collection; or as selector-scoped NOT_AUTHORED declarations, with no option REQUIRED on its own row. Optional and LOCAL later: an item alternativeGroup whose members keep RC-29 (NARROWS, never ENTAILS).
themeVerdict.why: No entry is a real schema gap. The one labelled STRUCTURAL (GF4 I02) is held with EXCLUSION COUNT items, as WIDEZONE-16.b is. RC-29 already makes unchosen alternatives on non-fillable rows NOT_AUTHORED(ALTERNATIVES), so a cross-row mechanism would change at most a reason code on the slice, never a status. It turns STRUCTURAL only if a cross-row choice were made to entail, or made free against SD-16. Christian's ruling, not a grammar need.

entries.minimalAmendment: New kind RELATIVE_BOUND, relation NARROWS: op (=,â‰ ,<,â‰¤,>,â‰¥) against another element's value on a named row, or a sum/spread over selector-matched elements at the item's scope, read from the stated game first (as RC-21). entries.reasoning: Not holdable: EQUALS needs a constant, FIELD items apply per element, only O1 aggregates (summing O3) and only POSITIONED reads another element. Team sizes are layout, so not boundary; not a missing list value. What 'Even numbers' means is KNOWLEDGE (ledgered), but either reading is relational. A whole-game count, not local numbers: inside the boundary. The STRUCTURAL worry fails: referent lookup exists (RC-21), the relation stays NARROWS, and once operands are read RC-27 sees an ordinary interval. Slice: 4+2>4 holds; P2/P5 stay NOT_AUTHORED.

entries.minimalAmendment: None beyond entry 16: P2[team=*] RELATIVE_BOUND spread(P2)=0, PREFERRED_DEFAULT, basis ASSUMED.

Near-inert: ASSUMED never entails and a departed PREFERRED_DEFAULT is ADAPTED, so it only changes a forward label; its sole evidence is an 'e.g.' already held inert by NEUTRAL-11.b (KNOWLEDGE, ledgered). entries.minimalAmendment: None. Declare E1 NON_CLAIMED (session-owned) with a note citing the Gate A performers-sum invariant; keep the engine-wording rule as a KNOWLEDGE ratification candidate.

A contract need not restate a universal Gate A invariant, and E1 is SESSION-only, so a selection item never sets it. ASSUMED anyway (bound only); the explicit rule is engine wording. entries.minimalAmendment: RELATIVE_BOUND with EXCLUSION strictness (EXCLUDES) on S6[noun=channel], OWN_INVOLVEMENT: forbidden value sum(S6 interval widths over the unit) >= E3. It must never entail a residual region (Â§5.2: residual space is not instantiated).

Not holdable: Gate A region fit is <=, not <; a 'central' exclusion over-restricts uneven channels; a residual S2 element would be INVENTED. Aggregate kind + existing EXCLUDES = LOCAL. entries.minimalAmendment: None now: record 03.a as OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY with the distinctness proxy as KNOWLEDGE. If a separation is ever authored, entry 16's RELATIVE_BOUND reading the other set members' O4 and O5 holds it (LOCAL).

The clause is ASSUMED, and Variable Target itself declares candidate separation NOT_AUTHORED (#7) and unconstrained. 'Not identical' is empty for physically distinct objects. entries.minimalAmendment: None. Restate I13 as P2[team=*] EQUALS {4, 6}, unordered, TYPICAL_EXAMPLE (as NEUTRAL-11.b holds its splits); 'can be introduced' is a permission, so no balance item. The session-goal condition is theme A (#51).

The knowledge requires no inequality: asymmetry 'can be introduced' is a permission, not a requirement; 'Uneven during transitions' is OB3, outside the boundary. GF4 is not in the slice.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: An item whose bound is read from other elements' stated values or from an aggregate over them. Items are unary per element; the only cross-element reads are POSITIONED relative terms (RC-21, positions only) and O1 summing O3. So equal or greater-than counts across teams with neutrals (P2, P5), and combined channel width against E3, cannot be written.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: One requirement kind, RELATIVE_BOUND, relation NARROWS (EXCLUDES under EXCLUSION): op in {=,â‰ ,<,<=,>,>=} against another named element's value on a named row, or a sum/spread over selector-matched elements at the item's scope, read from the stated game first (as RC-21). FIELD rows only; never entails a value or existence; not a fillable licence. Equally LOCAL alternative: new VIEW rows.
themeVerdict.why: The real entries (authored NEUTRAL-08.a; equality in GF2-14.b and NEUTRAL-09.a; WIDEZONE-09, which Â§5.2 names) fit a new kind with an existing relation: Â§6 LOCAL. NEUTRAL-10.a is Gate A's performers sum; I13 is inert; VARTARGET-03 is play. It turns STRUCTURAL only if it may ENTAIL by reference or entail existence (RC-2); the amendment forbids both. No slice verdict moves.

entries.minimalAmendment: Let J2 take a P4 role reference: register J2 valueType becomes 'object, region or performer-role reference', or add a field objectives[].roleReference, exclusive with J2. Limit spec Â§5.8's Gate A claim 'every member of its reference has a Space position' to object and region members.
entries.reasoning: Not holdable: rpc-library defines target_player as 'received and controlled by a designated target player', a P4 role. No object or region carries it, and a region reading would be invented. Not KNOWLEDGE (V1 lists it) and not outside the boundary (a designated role is layout; spec Â§5.3 expects roles to be referenced). A new reference type on an existing collection is LOCAL. The slice uses target_zone_entered and has no target player.

entries.minimalAmendment: None to the grammar. Choose a reading on existing selectors. Laws: trigger=OUT_END_LINE & qualifier.lastTouch=ATTACKING_TEAM (ASSUMED, like items 04-11). Practice: trigger=START, or * (T3-T5 are N/A under CONTINUE). Declare the trigger NOT_AUTHORED. If an unkeyed goal-kick element is still wanted: a label-only T1 field plus selector attribute (LOCAL). A label that entails T3-T6 values would be a new relation (STRUCTURAL).
entries.reasoning: The only authored text is 'Restart from goal kicks.', and L11 says 'goal kick' is undefined in every workbook. The drafter applies the Laws meaning to method, actor, awardee and place, but not to the trigger, though the Laws define a goal kick by its trigger, which T1 holds exactly (tr-OEL-att). Only which transitions are goal kicks stays unheld: a knowledge ambiguity. Dependents are ASSUMED or ENGINE_ONLY.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Put the NOT_AUTHORED declaration on O1 [kind=goal] (the open question is whether a goal stands at the kicking end) or on J1 [*]. A positional J1 attribute is unnecessary. It would also need a join through J2 to O4/S5.
entries.reasoning: It is declaration-only, on a question the knowledge leaves open: 'goal kick' is undefined (L11), and the original both non-claims J1 and leaves this open (L13). The object lets either team take the kick (05.a, T2 non-claim), so in a reciprocal game every end is some team's goal-kick end. J1 [*] therefore reaches what a positional selector would. On O1 [kind=goal] it reaches nothing in the slice, which has no goals.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Write the structural clause as an EXCLUSION: V11 [trigger=STANDING & effect=ACCESS] NOT_EXISTS, with V14a/V14b carrying team and region, or S4 functions âˆ‹ access forbidden, as WIDEZONE-08.a does. Basis ASSUMED, because 'no partition' is the original's reading. 'Removes direct contest' is OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY. An exact partition test belongs to theme C.
entries.reasoning: The premise is wrong twice. A team partition needs no team on the region, because ACCESS {team, region} carries it (spec Â§5.8: access and spatial advantage live in ACCESS). And ACCESS is not limited to event triggers, since STANDING is in the single closed trigger list that V12 uses (Â§5.7). The authored text (GAK-0106) concerns opportunity, which is outside the boundary. The slice has no ACCESS rule, so the exclusion holds.

entries.minimalAmendment: Add position.across as an S2 selector attribute, matched against register relative terms by the RC-21 interval test. Under RC-16 it narrows like âˆˆ and never entails. Write S2 [noun=channel & position.across=touchline-adjacent] at WHOLE_GAME. Bar OWN_INVOLVEMENT on COLLECTION items that entail. Reject 'contributing object': provenance held in the game feeds derivation back into matching, which is a STRUCTURAL change.
entries.reasoning: Not VOCABULARY: a 'wide channel' noun would put a relation in a noun, and spec Â§5.2 treats 'wide' as an interval comparison. Functions cannot separate wide channels from other channels. OWN_INVOLVEMENT is circular on 02.a, 03 and 08.d, because their scope depends on what they entail. A new selector attribute on an existing collection is LOCAL. The slice has exactly two channels, both wide (its centre is a corridor).

entries.minimalAmendment: Build on #29's attribute. Give the touchlines identities, either per-team relative terms ('touchline-adjacent, left/right of T's attack') or a neutral pair TOUCHLINE_1/TOUCHLINE_2 (VOCABULARY). Then write S2 [noun=channel & position.across=adjacent to touchline k] COUNT 1 for each k. Equivalent: a PER_TOUCHLINE scope whose unit is 'touches that touchline'. A new scope value is VOCABULARY under Â§6.
entries.reasoning: FIELD items apply to every match, so per-touchline relative terms alone cannot say 'one each'. COLLECTION existence selects only through selector attributes. Gate A's 'fit' does not rescue it: two non-overlapping channels can share one touchline by splitting its length (07's full length is only an ASSUMED default). A selector or scope over lateral side is needed, both LOCAL or VOCABULARY. The slice has one channel per touchline.

entries.minimalAmendment: Add condition.referents to V7's selectorAttributes (âˆ‹). Event referents are vocabulary tokens. Region/object referents use the same descriptions V8b values already use (VARTARGET-18.a, NEUTRAL-15.a), made contract-independent by #29. Not 'contributing object', which is STRUCTURAL. FIELD items may also use OWN_INVOLVEMENT once theme B lets Wide Zone entail its modifier.
entries.reasoning: Partly downstream of theme B. OWN_INVOLVEMENT is the spec's device for this case (Â§6: Wide Zone's multiplier coexisted 'only because each was object-scoped'), but it reaches nothing here. The advantage alternatives are TYPICAL_EXAMPLE, so no V7 element is entailed. Even when entailed, the entailing item cannot scope itself. A new selector attribute is LOCAL. The slice has one modifier (mod-wide).

entries.minimalAmendment: No selector attribute. Clarify RC-23 (derivation Â§5): 'a set's unit contains its J7 members and every element they reference through J2', as spec Â§5.5 implies ('a count range authored per set is checked per set'). Then 06.b's J1 [*] RANGE >=2 PER_OBJECTIVE_SET reaches exactly the set's member objectives. A 'set' attribute on J1 would duplicate J7 and still need this.
entries.reasoning: This is an ambiguity in the run's definition of a unit, not a missing attribute. Read strictly, RC-23 puts only referenced objects and regions in a unit, so 06.b reaches no objective. Unit membership is a scope matter (Â§6 treats scope values as VOCABULARY), not a relation or a status. It moves a slice verdict: only 06.b can entail the second candidate objective in the set 06.a entails, else INVENTED (J1 is not fillable). Christian decides.

entries.minimalAmendment: No register change. Clarify grammar Â§2: a FIELD row's selector uses its collection's selectorAttributes, as the syntax '<collection>[<attribute>=<value>].<field>' shows. Every other drafter already does so (S6 noun=, J2 role/team, T3-T6 trigger=, V17 subject=). 16.a becomes V17 [subject=live member of this set] at WHOLE_GAME.
entries.reasoning: V16-V22 inherit V15's 'subject' and J6-J12 inherit J5's 'scope'. Through subject, 16.a's forbidden STANDING reaches info-live only, never Wide Zone's rule, whose subject differs. OWN_INVOLVEMENT on FIELD items is not circular, because 06.a and 13.a entail the set and the rule. The only defect is Â§2's wording 'the row's selectorAttributes', an S2 risk. In the slice the two rules' subjects differ.

entries.minimalAmendment: Use #35's V7 attribute condition.referents (âˆ‹). I15 becomes V7 [condition.type=event & condition.referents âˆ‹ regain], and I14 selects on its own referent. No O1 change: I03 already holds the midline as two S2 halves.
entries.reasoning: The O1 half is already held: I03 keeps the midline off O1, and 'target' as line, zone or gate is a KNOWLEDGE ambiguity the drafter logged. The V7 half is real, because condition.type cannot separate two event modifiers. But I14 and I15 are TYPICAL_EXAMPLE and inert, so no verdict depends on their reach. A new selector attribute is LOCAL, so S4 holds for this entry. GF4 is not in the slice.

entries.minimalAmendment: None structural. State the association where it lives: P8 {group=TEAM_A, region=own-half-A} for the start area, and T4 references for restarts. 'Own half of T' resolves by position: the half touching the end T defends (RC-21 'own end'). Add the relative term 'own half (of team T)' (VOCABULARY, RPC-001 L-06). A stored region team would be a second place that can disagree (spec Â§5.6).
entries.reasoning: Team ownership of a half is derivable, not a property of the half. own-half-A spans 0-20 m from the west end line, and Team A defends west (J3 plus positions give DV1). The spec refuses to store direction for exactly this reason. The game needs the start placement on P8 and designation-based T4 references, both on existing rows. The restater put the association on the region instead.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: It lacks selector attributes that tell same-kind elements apart: lateral position (with touchline identity) on S2, and referents on V7. J2 cannot target a performer role. Two wording gaps put S2 at risk: Â§2 must say FIELD rows use their collection's attributes, and RC-23 must put J7 members in their set's unit. OWN_INVOLVEMENT is circular on items that entail their own elements.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: (1) S2 selector position.across, matched by RC-21 relative terms, narrowing under RC-16, plus per-touchline terms. (2) V7 selector condition.referents (âˆ‹). (3) J2 accepts P4 role references, with Â§5.8's position claim limited to objects and regions. (4) One-line clarifications to Â§2 and RC-23. (5) No OWN_INVOLVEMENT on entailing COLLECTION items. Never 'contributing object'.
themeVerdict.why: Of 11 entries, 5 are LOCAL gaps (#2, #29, #30, #35, #49), 5 are already holdable (#8, #11, #38, #42, #57) and 1 is KNOWLEDGE (#5). None adds a relation, status, strictness, value status, basis, declaration or area. The only STRUCTURAL risk is the drafters' optional 'contributing object' selector, which can be avoided. Only #38's RC-23 clarification moves a slice verdict, so it goes to Christian first.

entries.minimalAmendment: Register teamDesignations note: on a row not keyed by a trigger or episode, an episode or trigger designation in a selector is satisfied by every team that the game's stated transitions (T1/T2/T7, stated attributes per RC-1) make it at some START or trigger. An item binding only one episode also carries an episode scope (the L-05 VOCABULARY value).
entries.reasoning: Not holdable as written: designations are evaluated only at a trigger or episode, and P1/J1 elements carry TEAM_A/TEAM_B, so readers can match both teams, START's team only, or none (RC-22). RPC-001-03 alone fits selector * (RC-19 makes every team ATTACKING_TEAM sometime). The rule fixes a selector value's meaning, like RC-21/22; matching on verdicts would be STRUCTURAL. It settles L40/L43 and 11.a's reach to L85/L89 (KR-03): Christian first.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Add tautological items J4[role=PRIMARY_SCORING] EQUALS PRIMARY_SCORING and S4[functions âˆ‹ objective-area] EQUALS objective-area (that member line), so both rows are CLAIMED by items; RC-16 already entails the same values.

The missing J1 reference attribute behind GF2-08.b's workaround is a selector-attribute question (theme D). The declarations as written are also correct: J4 lines stay ENTAILED via GF2-08.a.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Write the universal as an exclusion: J8[*] EQUALS 0, strictness EXCLUSION, WHOLE_GAME. With no set the forbidden value is absent, so the forward result is SATISFIED; UNMET applies only to REQUIRED items (RC-35).
entries.reasoning: liveCardinality is a non-negative integer, so '>= 1 for every set' is exactly 'no set has 0'. As a RANGE on non-fillable J8 the item supported nothing anyway (NARROWS), so no support is lost, and VARTARGET-07's J8 = 1 neither collides with nor violates the exclusion. No derivation change is needed. The slice has set-A and set-B, so the item is not vacuous there.

entries.minimalAmendment: RC-11 gains a complement Â¬(selector), satisfied by every element that fails the inner selector, including one lacking the attribute. It fixes no attribute under RC-16, like âˆˆ. It may be limited to declaration selectors (RC-13).
entries.reasoning: Partly holdable: for single-valued closed lists the complement is an âˆˆ enumeration (GF2's O1). Not for set-valued S4 functions or unstated attributes, so S2-S4 fall back to NON_CLAIMED(*) over the target, and rule 4's 'declares NON_CLAIMED' can be read as permission against the contract's own ENTAILS item. An operator is on neither Â§6 list; like a new attribute it adds no relation. No slice region is objective-area, so nothing moves.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Â§4 asks for 'at least one' declaration per row, so CLAIMED with NON_CLAIMED is already allowed. CLAIMED alone also works: RC-28 makes TYPICAL_EXAMPLE inert (no bound), so derivation rule 4 finds nothing to bar. Optionally note this beside RC-7.
entries.reasoning: No declaration-mechanism change: several declarations per row are used throughout (GF2 O1 and J1, RPC-001 J3). The item supports, bounds and collides with nothing, so either declaration gives the same verdicts. E2 and E3 are SESSION rows with no fillable entry, so no free choice arises on the slice.

entries.minimalAmendment: Same as entry 18: a complement Â¬(selector) in RC-11, true of elements failing the inner selector including those lacking the attribute, fixing no attribute under RC-16.
entries.reasoning: Partly holdable: V6 was done by âˆˆ over the rest of the closed V4 list, and J1 needs no carve-out since NEUTRAL-17.a acts as an exclusion whatever overlaps it. V8b 'other referents' is per-member selection (theme D), not negation. The residue is P4 roleName (open list) and P8-P10 group, where UNDECLARED(*) wrongly bars choice on neutral elements the object non-claims. None of these rows is fillable and no neutral placement exists.

entries.minimalAmendment: None needed. Optional register clarification: V5 (and V8b, T4, P10) references may name an SV1 implicit fraction, which exists by SD-12 without an S2 element.
entries.reasoning: Spec Â§5.2: implicit halves and thirds 'exist without declaration' and are never instantiated as marked regions; Â§5.8 needs condition referents to be existing regions. An SV1 half is one (half is on the S3 noun list), so PCG-06 with PCG-07 already holds 'in their half'. A reference is not support, so views still support no stored row. No slice V5 item names an SV1 fraction; the game's halves are S2 elements.

entries.minimalAmendment: Run convention beside RC-6: an item whose checkability is OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY takes row NONE and requirement N/A. It stays inert (RC-31); only its form changes.
entries.reasoning: Grammar Â§1 already records such items as OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY and says they are not forced onto a row; Â§3's required row and requirement fields simply lack an N/A. That is a drafting inconsistency, not a missing row, field or kind. Restaters diverged (nearest row in RPC-001, NONE in NEUTRAL and GF4, a dash in PCG), but RC-31 makes every form inert, so no line or forward result differs.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. State example-only existence as COUNT (or RANGE >= 1) on the COLLECTION row. That carries a value, so it may be TYPICAL_EXAMPLE: V7[condition.type=event] COUNT 1 TYPICAL_EXAMPLE, and V23[startsOn=POSSESSION_CHANGE] likewise.
entries.reasoning: Â§2 lets COUNT/RANGE state existence. RC-6 forces N/A only on items with no value, and RC-28 then makes the item inert, which is exactly 'example only'. No new value status is needed, so the STRUCTURAL label fails. As drafted, I17 (AUTHORED, SUPPORTING, EXISTS on V7) would entail a modifier's existence under RC-2, an over-entailment. GF4 is a blind contract, not in the slice.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Recommendations and fit scores are cross-object selection knowledge; a contract states what one object requires in a game. A requirement GA-001 imposes is written as GF4's own item citing GA-001, as RPC-001-01.a, RPC-001-14.a and GF2-09 did.
entries.reasoning: The contract touches the game only through item matching and non-claim permission (Â§6); an object-to-object link touches neither, and Â§7 excludes selection scores. Relationship rules exist only to decide collisions on one row, and 'recommended with' decides none. A link's requirement content is holdable today by citation, so no relation is needed and the STRUCTURAL label fails. No slice object depends on a link.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Drop the exclusion prose from the restated game. The contracts hold it: WIDEZONE-08.a (no access function on channels), 08.b (no ACCESS consequence on a channel), 08.c. 'Entry never compulsory' is route and play, outside the boundary.
entries.reasoning: Spec Â§5.8 removes exclusions[] from the representation: they live in the contract and are checked by Gate B. The game states only what exists, and under the existence rule an unstated restriction, access consequence or compulsory-entry rule cannot exist without entailed support. The restater's own note cites Â§5.8. Nothing is lost: each clause has a contract EXCLUSION item or is play.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Contract exclusions hold it: RPC-001-12 and GF2-20 (retention as V1), WIDEZONE-16.a (channel as J2) and 16.b, VARTARGET-12.a (a second route). A01-02-12.a/b (goal kick) rest on ENGINE_ONLY: a KNOWLEDGE gap, not schema.
entries.reasoning: Same design rule (Â§5.8): the game holds one primary event (SD-06) and its objectives, anything else is simply absent, and Gate B checks the contract EXCLUSION items against it. The goal-kick clause is inert only because its basis is engine wording (SD-21); ratifying that wording, not changing the grammar, would cure it.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. NEUTRAL-15.a (neutral involvement as a modifier referent) and VARTARGET-18.a (a candidate member as a referent) hold the first two clauses. 'Retention may not outweigh progression' is incentive balance, recorded inert in GF2-21 (OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY).
entries.reasoning: Â§5.8 keeps exclusions out of the game, and SD-06 restricts V7: a value change must be explicitly authored, so an absent modifier needs no row to stay absent. The only clause no row could hold, 'outweigh', concerns the incentive landscape, which Â§7 keeps outside the representation.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: Two selector-level reading rules: how an episode or trigger team designation (BUILD_OUT_TEAM, ATTACKING_TEAM) is satisfied on a row with no trigger or episode, and a complement operator for open-listed, set-valued or unstated selector attributes. Every other entry is holdable today or deliberately outside the representation. Both drafter STRUCTURAL labels (53, 54) fail on verification.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: (1) A teamDesignations note: on a static row, an episode or trigger designation is satisfied by each team that the game's stated transitions make it at some START or trigger, or the item takes an episode scope. (2) RC-11 gains Â¬(selector), true of elements failing the inner selector, including those lacking the attribute, fixing none under RC-16. Housekeeping: row NONE and requirement N/A for OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY items.
themeVerdict.why: Both real gaps meet Â§6 LOCAL: they fix selector meaning and add no relation, status, strictness, value-status, basis, declaration type, source kind or area. Unamended, matching stays non-deterministic on static-row designations and on overlapping declarations. Rule (1) moves slice lines L40/L43 (P3) and 11.a's reach to team B's objectives under KR-03, so it goes to Christian before incorporation.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. The retreat non-claim sits on V11/V13/V14b (effect=ACCESS on the restart triggers) and on T2-T5 for out of play. RPC-001 already declares NON_CLAIMED(*) there, and From Goal Kicks places the same question there. The touch-limit non-claim needs no row. If the #17 row is adopted, RPC-001 adds NON_CLAIMED on it.
entries.reasoning: A non-claim is only a permission check on REALIZATION values on a registered path (spec Â§3), and S3 coverage is per register row. A retreat line is an ACCESS consequence on the restart trigger, which RPC-001 already non-claims (V13 note: access and eligibility are free). A touch limit has no row, so no free choice can create one (SD-16) and no text may describe one (SD-05). The non-claim has nothing to permit, and no line is touched.

entries.minimalAmendment: A new COLLECTION row in Performers, e.g. performers.actionRules[] (selectorAttributes: group, action), with FIELD rows .group (team designation, role or NEUTRALS), .action (draft list: touch, pass, receive, contest) and .limit. GF2-22 and GF2-15's clause become EXCLUSION NOT_EXISTS items (EXCLUDES). No fillable entry. GF2-22 should be PARTLY_STRUCTURAL, because 'passing options' are affordances.
entries.reasoning: Not holdable: V4 eligibility binds only the primary event, and forbidding it would bar incentives GF2-22 allows. S4 access and V11 ACCESS hold only region limits. Not out by design: Â§1 holds what the rules key on, and Â§7 does not list rules. LOCAL: existing kinds, relations, statuses and RC-2 existence. The slice game holds no such rule, so there are no lines and GF2-22 is SATISFIED either way. GF2-15's remainder is play plus an ASSUMED polarity.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Re-place NEUTRAL-05.a as P5 RANGE >= 1 (as NEUTRAL-01.a does); NEUTRAL-03.a/.b and 14.a/.b carry the 'permanent advantage'. The 'not rotated, not waiting' clause needs no row, because the representation cannot express either.
entries.reasoning: The authored words ('permanent numerical advantage for whichever side has the ball', 'live numerical overload') are held by P5 >= 1 and P6a STANDING / P6b ATTACKING_TEAM. 'Whole activity, outfield, not rotated or waiting' is a gloss from the prose-era contract. It is true by construction: one continuous game, a fixed partition (E1 = teams + neutrals), and no inactive state. Only the item's own forward result changes (unplaced to SATISFIED); no line verdict does.

entries.minimalAmendment: None of its own. If the #17 row is adopted, the Neutral contract declares it NON_CLAIMED (or NOT_AUTHORED) for group=NEUTRALS. Pressing, tackling and dispossession stay OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY.
entries.reasoning: Nothing is authored and nothing is needed. NOT_AUTHORED means the object needs the row filled (sheet Â§4), and a game with neutrals is complete without protection or a touch limit. Pressing and tackling are play, as the drafter agrees. The missing row is the #17 gap seen from the declaration side and adds no failure: no game can contain such a rule (SD-16, SD-05), so the open question reaches no line.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Which individuals wear the neutral bibs is not game structure. Rounds and periods belong to the separate period-structure entry (GF2 ledger 'E4, J3, DV1'), not to this theme.
entries.reasoning: The spec holds performers as counts, affiliation and distinguishability (Â§5.3), never as individual players. No rule keys on who a neutral is, so rotating players between rounds changes no row. Rounds themselves are period structure, a separate ledger item. Rotation is also unauthored and is not a value the object needs, so no declaration is owed and no line is affected.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. The game's P5 (L45, value 2), P6a (L46) and P6b (L47) lines hold the positive content. 'Never fixed to one team' is P6b's value stated as a negation. 'Not rotated' is an exclusion, and by design the game holds no exclusions (spec Â§5.8).
entries.reasoning: P5, P6a and P6b state two neutrals whose affiliation follows possession. 'Persistent active outfield' is true by construction: one period, a fixed partition, no inactive state. The negations are exclusions. Â§5.8 removed exclusions[] from the game: they live in NEUTRAL-04 and NEUTRAL-05, and Gate B checks them. The game's P6a/P6b values differ from the contract's, but that is a derivation matter, not this entry.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Keep the exclusion in GF2-18's contract (OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY: reciprocal influence is play). Its structural effect is already held on T2/T6 (GF2-07.b forbids giving the ball back to LOST_BALL; GF2-17 sets CONTINUE on POSSESSION_CHANGE) and by J1 objectives for both teams.
entries.reasoning: A game statement that something is absent is an exclusion. Â§5.8 deliberately removed exclusions[] from the representation: contracts hold them and Gate B checks them. What a turn structure would change (who gets the ball after an attempt, whether play stops) sits on T2/T6/T7, which the game states (L153, L157, L158). Queued or waiting players cannot be represented at all. No verdict changes.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: A home for standing rules on what players may do, or on their status, outside the primary event's conditions: touch limits, banned receivers, pass-direction bans, rules stopping a team contesting the ball, protected status, and later EM-0007 participation state. Region restrictions already fit S4 access + V11 ACCESS (as Wide Zone did). Pass rules tied to scoring fit V3-V6 (as Pass Combination Gate did). Players' persistence holds by construction.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: One new COLLECTION row in Performers, performers.actionRules[] (selectorAttributes: group, action), with FIELD rows .group, .action (a draft closed list) and .limit. Existence follows RC-2; no fillable entry; items use existing kinds (EQUALS/RANGE/NOT_EXISTS). A trigger for breaking a rule, if ever authored, is VOCABULARY. Every contract then declares the new row (S3).
themeVerdict.why: Only #17 is a real gap, and its fix is LOCAL: an added row using existing kinds, relations, statuses and derivation. No hidden STRUCTURAL step was found. The other six entries are already held, out of scope by design, or unauthored. The run used action rules only as exclusions, and SD-16 and SD-05 already keep such rules out of every game, so no slice line verdict changes. A rule authored later would fail Gate B visibly, not be lost silently.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Record the declaration as NOT_AUTHORED on T5 for the goal-kick element (RC-7, beside A01-02-04.b): how the ball is put back into play, including when it is live, is what the P-1 method list types. A fixed variant, if ever authored, is VOCABULARY on that draft list (SD-18). Only a region-parameterised liveness rule would need a field, and n7's optional restriction element can carry it.
entries.reasoning: Only a notAuthored declaration exists; nothing is authored. The declaration mechanism holds it (T5 or T6 with a note, RC-7). Slice: goal-kick T6 lines are ENTAILED by GF2-16.b on OUT_*, and otherwise NOT_AUTHORED because A01-02-04.a/.b are ASSUMED (START_PROCEDURE, POST_SCORE). Moving the declaration shifts at most a reason code, not a verdict.

entries.minimalAmendment: Optional transitions[].placement.restrictions[] {group: team designation, region | minDistance_m from the placement}: a new COLLECTION row under Transitions. It exists only where an authored item entails it (absent = none imposed). Sitting under .placement, the existing CONTINUE coherence rule makes it N/A; metres fall under P-4's existing 'metres'. It also covers n9 and the restart-keyed part of n63.
entries.reasoning: V11 ACCESS is only approximate: regions are fixed layout, a distance from a mobile placement is not a region, and consequences have no end (Â§5.8 removed duration). P8 places groups at START only. A clearance or retreat rule (a build-out line) is a dead-ball rule a coach lays out, inside the boundary. EQUALS/RANGE only: LOCAL. It must stay optional: if required whenever STOP_RESUME, every slice restart gains a NOT_AUTHORED line.

entries.minimalAmendment: Same optional element as n7, with a playedTo {region} field (the ball's first destination), existing only where authored. 'Short or long', 'to which player', 'how many passes' and 'along the ground' stay OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY (play).
entries.reasoning: Only a non-claim ('All free'), vacuous today: SD-16 bars a free choice from creating such a rule, and no row lets knowledge require one. The 'to which zone' clause is a rule keyed on the ball entering a region, the kind of fact REGION_ENTRY keys on, so it is inside the boundary. No existing row holds it: T4 is where the restart is taken from, not where it goes. LOCAL; no slice line exists for it.

entries.minimalAmendment: timeWindows[].endsOn (a trigger list from the closed vocabulary, as an alternative to duration), so a temporary effect ends on a trigger through the window's existing expiryEffect; and cap {count, per EPISODE|GAME} on valueModifiers[] and consequences[]. Both optional, existing only where authored. Do not reinstate consequences[].duration, which Â§5.8 removed deliberately.
entries.reasoning: Not holdable: V11 has no end; windows end by duration only; a reversing consequence on POSSESSION_CHANGE would fire in states with no advantage, failing 'every referent resolves in every state'; nothing caps frequency. These are rules governing state, not state, so inside the boundary. New fields on existing collections: LOCAL. Declarations only; the only persistence text is engine wording. Slice mod-wide stays NOT_AUTHORED (notAuthored #1, #2).

entries.minimalAmendment: value.primaryEvent.conditions[].resetOn: a list of triggers from the closed vocabulary, one property per trigger (as J10), added to RC-15's list-valued rows. PCG-05 then splits into typed items: resetOn contains POSSESSION_CHANGE, OUT_END_LINE and OUT_TOUCHLINE.
entries.reasoning: Authored: 'Pass count resets when possession is lost or the ball leaves play.' V6 holds it only as a compound string that RC-34 can match verbatim. Its triggers are hidden in prose, against Â§3's atomic properties and the single closed trigger vocabulary, so Gate A cannot check them. Episodes do not substitute: OUT_* begin none under SD-14, which does not reinitialise requirements. New field, EQUALS: LOCAL. PCG is not in the slice.

entries.minimalAmendment: valueModifiers[].condition.value (the V6 analogue for modifiers), holding 'the regain began the scoring team's current episode', with V8b = {regain} only; the modified event is the primary event by construction. 'Shot' as its own rewarded event is barred by SD-06 (a second way to score); as the event kind it is VOCABULARY.
entries.reasoning: Partly holdable: V8b can name the regain, and the later event is always the modified primary event, so order is implicit. What is missing is the link 'in the same episode' (SD-14: POSSESSION_CHANGE begins one); without it, 'a regain occurred' is vacuous. No row carries a parameter on a modifier condition. New field on an existing collection: LOCAL. I15 is TYPICAL_EXAMPLE, so inert; GF4 is not in the slice.

entries.minimalAmendment: None (schema). Restate the game's neutrals as P6a = STANDING and P6b = ATTACKING_TEAM, as NEUTRAL-03 and NEUTRAL-14 already do. ATTACKING_TEAM is re-evaluated each episode, so START (Team A) and each restart's awardee are covered without a second pair. Flag STANDING's gloss ('openly known information') for the SD-18 review; C4 stays open.
entries.reasoning: The game's own words, 'always play for the team currently in possession', are a standing rule; the restater chose the consequence reading. No amendment is needed, but the restatement matters: POSSESSION_CHANGE/WON_BALL fails NEUTRAL-03.a/.b and 14.a/.b (EQUALS), so P6a/P6b lose support and those items read VIOLATED. STANDING/ATTACKING_TEAM makes them ENTAILED. Report this to the derivers.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. The placed 'group' is a formation of players (the first defenders' line), which Â§5.3 makes NOT_AUTHORED and never inferred. Its placement sources are ENGINE_ONLY (RPC-001-04.a-c). The between-description can be written as two 'beyond' tests (as RPC-001-04.b does). A restart retreat rule with a region, if ever authored, is n7's LOCAL amendment.
entries.reasoning: P8 is START-only by design. The game's 'at every restart the defending team has a line positioned between...' ('not marked; only determinable') says where defenders are during play. It is not a rule a coach lays out. Its sources are engine wording (inert, SD-21) and RPC-001-18.d's outside clause. Extending P8 to restarts changes nothing: the element stays NOT_AUTHORED(ENGINE_ONLY) or INVENTED.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. 'No opponent retreat or exclusion distance is authored by any selection, so none is imposed' is reconciler rationale about an absence. The game holds nothing, and Gate B reverse has nothing to check. Reclassify it with the restater's 'rationale prose' KNOWLEDGE entry. The row a retreat rule would need, if one were authored, is n7's.
entries.reasoning: The representation holds supported facts; an absence is represented by absence, and SD-16 forbids a free choice creating the rule anyway. The same restater classed comparable reconciliation prose as KNOWLEDGE (outside the boundary). This is the game-side duplicate of n7 and should not be counted twice.

entries.minimalAmendment: None (schema). Restate it as its own T1 element: trigger=REGION_ENTRY, trigger.region in {the candidate zones, held as S2 regions per Â§5.2}, with T2-T7 copied from tr-OEL-att. Under RC-19 a REGION_ENTRY element exists only where authored, and none is, so it is INVENTED: spec Â§9's expected catch. Folding it into tr-OEL-att hides it.
entries.reasoning: No row equating two triggers is needed: a separate element carries the same restart values. The 'inactive' restriction depends on which target is live now (Â§7, state in progress). That does not matter here, because the element has no support at all (VARTARGET-12 supports only 'carries no value'). Folded in, the invented trigger escapes Gate B reverse, the Â§3 failure. The restatement must change; the schema need not.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: Optional rule fields keyed on the closed trigger vocabulary. (1) At a restart: rules on non-acting groups and on the ball's destination (clearance or retreat, playedTo), since P8 is START-only and T3-T5 hold only actor, spot and method. (2) The lifecycle of value rules: a condition's reset triggers, an effect or window that ends on a trigger, and a per-episode cap. (3) A same-episode link for event referents in modifier conditions.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: One reusable trigger-list field type (as J10: closed triggers, one property per trigger), used in optional fields on existing collections: conditions[].resetOn; timeWindows[].endsOn; cap {count, per EPISODE|GAME} on valueModifiers[] and consequences[]; valueModifiers[].condition.value; transitions[].placement.restrictions[] {group, region | minDistance_m, playedTo}. Each exists only where authored; the RC-15 and RC-20 lists are extended.
themeVerdict.why: Every real gap is a new optional field or collection row on an existing collection, using EQUALS/RANGE/COUNT (ENTAILS or NARROWS). None needs a new relation, status, strictness, valueStatus, basis, declaration or source kind. None changes a slice verdict: each is declaration-only or outside the slice. Keep the fields optional, and do not reinstate consequences[].duration. The verdict-relevant findings are restatement errors (n61, n66).

entries.minimalAmendment: None for the eight contracts. Place GF2-01 as E2 EXISTS and E3 EXISTS (REQUIRED, AUTHORED, note: one length x width rectangle by construction). It is then always SATISFIED, as RC-19's reachable triggers exist by construction. Only if EM-0001's authored Shape (EMP-0007) is ever contracted: a FIELD row E5 envelope.area.shape, LOCAL (see #37).
entries.reasoning: E2 and E3 are non-collection FIELD rows, so every representable game has exactly one area and it is a length x width rectangle. 'A single rectangular playing area' can never be violated, so placing it as field presence on E2/E3 loses nothing and moves no line (the session still supports E2/E3). 'No other layout can be represented' is true, but only knowledge that authors other shapes needs one, and none of the eight contracts does.

entries.minimalAmendment: Shared with #31: two register relative terms, 'longitudinal' (the element's along-extent >= its across-extent) and 'lateral' (the reverse), usable with POSITIONED or ORIENTED on S5/S6 and O4/O5, relation NARROWS as now. GF2-05.b then reads S6 ORIENTED lateral.
entries.reasoning: The premise is wrong: nothing restricts ORIENTED to DV1, and spec 3 tests ORIENTED on 'the position interval'. The real gap is that the register split position into S5 and S6, so no defined test says which way an element runs. For GF2 nothing authored hinges on it: the item is ASSUMED ('the text never states an orientation'), SUPPORTING, and its S2 objective-area selector matches no slice element (the targets are O1).

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Coverage is per register row (S3), and NON_CLAIMED on E4, J3 and DV1 with notes carries it. A property with no row can be neither claimed nor filled, so the non-claim's only job, permitting a REALIZATION value (spec 3), has nothing to act on.
entries.reasoning: Period structure is not a game property: E4 is one session-owned duration. Changing ends would make direction vary over time, which SD-07's stable direction and a static J3 exclude by design. GF2 claims nothing on either, so no item, bound or permission is lost. If a future object authored periods or an end switch, that would be a positive claim needing a home, not this non-claim.

entries.minimalAmendment: Add register relative terms 'longitudinal' (element's along-extent >= its across-extent) and 'lateral' (the reverse) for POSITIONED/ORIENTED on S5/S6 and O4/O5, relation NARROWS. WIDEZONE-04.b: S5 POSITIONED longitudinal, selector noun=channel. Equal-rank alternative: a VIEW row space.regions[].orientation computed from S5/S6. Not a stored field (see reasoning).
entries.reasoning: 'Along both touchlines' authors that channels run with the axis. Once WIDEZONE-07 (ASSUMED full length) is adapted, touchline-adjacent plus a 6-10 m across-width still admit an 8 m stub, and no one-row bound says along >= across. LOCAL: existing kind and relation, and POSITIONED already reads other intervals. The drafter's stored field hides cost: it would need support or a new fillable kind under unruled P-4. Slice channels 40x6 m: SATISFIED.

entries.minimalAmendment: None for the eight contracts: E2 and E3 NON_CLAIMED carry it, because the register represents one rectangle only. If EM-0001's Shape is contracted: FIELD row E5 envelope.area.shape (session default rectangular), noting that relative terms, SV1 and SD-11 are defined only for rectangles. LOCAL: a new row in an existing area.
entries.reasoning: A non-claim over a property no contract can claim and no realization can fill has nothing to permit, so nothing is lost. The drafter is right that EM-0001 authors Shape (EMD-0003; EMP-0007 lists circular, triangular, irregular), so that object's knowledge would not fit, but no selected object carries it. Hidden cost checked: the session already owns the area, so E5 needs no new source kind; extending E1-E4 to E5 follows the area.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. The game states what exists; 'no partition' is an exclusion, and spec 5.8 removes exclusions[] from the representation (they live in contracts and Gate B checks them). A partition would show as an access-function region or an ACCESS consequence, and the game lists neither. The 'area' S2 element duplicates the envelope and should not be a region.
entries.reasoning: 'Shared occupancy' is where players may be during play, outside the boundary. 'No partition or separating boundary' is a negative the game holds by absence, with Gate B reverse catching any invented access region. The restater also made the whole area an S2 region with an off-list noun and no function, against spec 5.2 ('every instantiated region serves at least one supported function'); E2 x E3 already holds it.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. SD-12 draws the line: halves and thirds are 'derived views, not marked regions', so marked = an instantiated S2 region or O1 object, determinable but unmarked = SV1. RPC-001-06 already used it. Only if Christian rules that Wide Zone's 'Zones optional' makes channel marking optional would a field regions[].marked be needed (LOCAL).
entries.reasoning: Each case has a home. Own halves that 'need not be marked' are SV1 per team, referenced by P10 (views 'exist without declaration', spec 5.2). The 'unmarked' corridor is residual space, which 5.2 says is not instantiated. The 'not marked' defending line is a formation of players (5.3: NOT_AUTHORED). 'Marked' target zones are O1 objects. The gap comes from the restater putting own halves and corridor in S2.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Revision 3 removed objects[].owner on purpose: for scoring references it duplicated objectives[].team, and for the ball it was game-in-progress state. The zone owner is J3 through J2, which the game already states (L79, L87). A change of ball owner is the POSSESSION_CHANGE transition, as GF2-07.a restated it.
entries.reasoning: The entry's own detail concedes that the zone owner duplicates J3. 'The team currently in possession; ownership changes through opposed play' is the state of a game in progress, which the boundary excludes; its rule-relevant part, that possession can change, is a reachable T1 element (RC-19). Revision 4 keeps objects without owner, so this is one home per fact by design, not an omission.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. The neutrals' direction is derived, not stored: P6a STANDING and P6b ATTACKING_TEAM (NEUTRAL-03, NEUTRAL-14) say whom they play for, and DV1 gives that team's direction. NEUTRAL-04.a forbids P6b = DEFENDING_TEAM ('never defend'); NEUTRAL-17.a forbids any J1 objective of their own, so DV1 computes no neutral entry.
entries.reasoning: DV1 is per team because only teams attack objectives (J3). A group with no objective has no direction of its own by computation, and 'attacks whichever end its team attacks' is player movement during play, outside the boundary. Storing a neutral direction would create a second place that can disagree, which spec 5.6 rejects for direction. The game's P6a/P6b values (L46-L47) are a separate, trigger-keyed theme.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: A defined test for which way a region or object runs. Elements are axis-aligned intervals split over S5/S6 (O4/O5), and ORIENTED has a comparison only on DV1, so 'along both touchlines' (WIDEZONE-04) cannot be required once full length is adapted. Latent only: an envelope shape row for EM-0001's authored Shape (EMP-0007). None of the eight contracts selects it.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: Add two register relative terms, 'longitudinal' (the element's along-extent >= its across-extent) and 'lateral' (the reverse), usable with POSITIONED/ORIENTED on S5/S6 and O4/O5, relation NARROWS unchanged. An equivalent is a VIEW row space.regions[].orientation. The other seven entries need no amendment. Add E5 envelope.area.shape only when EM-0001 is contracted.
themeVerdict.why: Only the orientation pair (#13, #31) is a real gap, and it is LOCAL under grammar 6 (an existing kind and relation, or a new row in an existing area). It changes no slice verdict. The rest are held by construction (E2 x E3), by SD-12's S2/SV1 split, by J3 and P6a/P6b, or are kept out of the game by design (exclusions, ball ownership, play). Nothing needs a new relation, status or derivation change.

entries.minimalAmendment: Add FIELD row V8c value.valueModifiers[].condition.value: the predicate or parameter of a modifier's condition (a qualitative term or threshold, e.g. 'starts in or moves through'), SELECTION, not fillable, derived as V6 is (RC-5: an EQUALS verbatim term ENTAILS; SD-15 FREE(b) not extended). Gate A's modifier-overlap test should then read V8c with V8b.
entries.reasoning: Not holdable: V8a types only the referent kind and V8b lists referents, so 'starts in or moves through' (wide) and 'scored from' (deep tiers) become one property and the renderer could supply either (SD-05). V8a=event with REGION_ENTRY covers only 'moves through'. Inside the boundary: V4-V6 already hold origin/progression terms for primary events. LOCAL under Â§6: new field on V7, EQUALS/ENTAILS, no new relation, status or value.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Optional sheet note: objects and their O4/O5 positions are static and target availability's only home is assignmentRule (Â§5.8), so 'stays present' is met by O1 EXISTS (02.a); closing a region-type candidate is excludable on V14b as WIDEZONE-08.b does. Only if SD-18 adds an object-changing V13 effect would an object referent on V14 be needed (LOCAL).
entries.reasoning: Positive clause placed (02.a). The negative clause (not removed, closed or relocated on account of liveness) cannot be violated by any game on the register: V13 is closed (ACCESS, COUNT_CHANGE) and names no object, O4/O5 hold one interval, and Â§5.8 homes liveness only in J11. The vacuity the drafter notes is the grammar's guarantee, not a loss: an unviolable exclusion needs no row.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. Record the gate at WHOLE_GAME: it gates the one primary event, credited to the team that achieves it (Â§5.8), so 'the attacking team's passes' is that team by construction. Keep V6 for the threshold (PCG-04); a team term on V6 beside a RANGE item invites a V6 collision. Only a one-team condition would need a V3 team selector attribute (LOCAL); none of the eight contracts authors one.
entries.reasoning: A team field would hold a constant: conditions attach to the primary event, whose scorer is the team whose passes count, and SCORING_TEAM/ATTACKING_TEAM are evaluated at the event (sheet Â§2). The drafter's PER_TEAM is what fails: V3 elements carry no J3/P1/T2 designation, so RC-23 puts them in no team unit. Who passes during play is outside the boundary. All RPC-001 conditions are WHOLE_GAME.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. The functional content is held: PCG-10/11 (the count is shown), V22 ALL, and V17 STANDING versus a per-pass reveal (off-list trigger, RC-33). If Christian wants a mode held, IE-D004 ACCESS_MODE as a sixth V row is LOCAL (the five-dimension cap is the specification's own), but both media map to DIRECT, so it would not separate them.
entries.reasoning: 'Count out loud or use a counter' is how the coach delivers information; no rule keys on the medium, and spec Â§1 and Â§7 keep coach behaviour and language out. Unlike P7 bibs, which make a structural role perceivable, the medium changes no structure; its one functional difference (per pass vs continuous) already has V17. As a non-fillable row, RC-29 would block every PCG game on a coach-delivery choice.

entries.minimalAmendment: None. The Variable Target restatement already places each clause: in-play re-assignment as J11a EXISTS on in-play keys (08.a); 'changes at least once' OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY (08.b); 'not determinable before the trigger' as V17 EXCLUSION of STANDING (16.a) plus OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY (16.b); independence NON_CLAIMED on J11a. The game holds resolved J10/J11/J12 values, not requirements.
entries.reasoning: These are requirement prose from the old game's 'state' field, not game properties: a game holds the resolved rule (J10 triggers, J11a keys, J11b yields, J12) and requirements live in contracts (spec Â§6). The VARTARGET restater placed every clause on existing rows or as OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY. Independence holds by construction (each set has its own J11 map; a coupled J11b procedure is excludable). The game restater misfiled them.

entries.minimalAmendment: The same V8c field as entry 34, nothing more. The beneficiary needs no field: Â§5.8 removed valueModifiers[].beneficiary on purpose, because a modifier changes the primary event's value, which is credited to the team that achieves it; a neutral is not a team and cannot be credited.
entries.reasoning: Two halves. Beneficiary: OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY_BY_DESIGN (deliberately removed in Â§5.8; the acting team is the scoring team by construction). Path: the same gap as entry 34, LOCAL. On the slice, V8c adds one line for mod-wide (ENTAILED once WIDEZONE-11 sits on it); no existing line changes, and mod-wide stays blocked by Wide Zone's declared NOT_AUTHORED on V7 existence and V9 magnitude.

themeVerdict.whatTheGrammarLacks: One field: value-modifier conditions (V7-V10) hold only the referent kind (V8a) and referents (V8b), so how the qualifying action must relate to the referent ('starts in or moves through' versus 'scored from') has no home; primary-event conditions have V6 for this. The other four entries are held by existing rows, deliberately outside the boundary, or vacuous by construction.
themeVerdict.smallestAmendmentForTheTheme: Add FIELD row V8c value.valueModifiers[].condition.value (predicate or parameter; SELECTION; not fillable), derived exactly as V6 under RC-5 with SD-15 unchanged, and have Gate A's overlap test read it with V8b. It would also give GF4's 'regain leading to shot' a home. No relation, status, strictness, value status, basis, declaration or source-kind change.
themeVerdict.why: Only 34 and 69's path half are real, and they are one LOCAL gap under sheet Â§6: a new field on an existing collection using EQUALS/ENTAILS. It changes no existing slice line (it adds one ENTAILED line to mod-wide, which stays blocked by declared gaps), so it can be listed as a LOCAL amendment rather than precede design. Nothing here meets any STRUCTURAL criterion.
